newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea June CPI rises 4.0 pct vs 5.5 pct yr ago. [CORRECTED 08:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: S.Korea June CPI rises 4.0 pct vs 5.5 pct yr ago. [CORRECTED 08:55 GMT]

text.p: South Korea's consumer price index (CPI) rose 4.0 percent in June (corrects from July) on the year, down from a 5.5 percent rise a year earlier, Ministry of Finance and Economy figures showed on Tuesday.
(base=1995 for June and May '97, and 1990 for June '96)
A ministry official said the CPI in June slowed thanks to stability in prices of farm goods and some industrial goods.
Prices for agricultural, livestock and fisheries products rose 1.6 percent year-on-year in the month.
Prices for industrial products rose a year-on-year 4.1 percent, led by a 26.5 percent rise in oil products.
But industrial product prices, excluding oil products, rose year-on-year 1.4 percent, the ministry said.
The official said intensifying competition in distribution helped keep industrial prices in check.
Prices for personal computers fell 14.6 percent, and those for television sets dropped 6.4 percent, the ministry said.
Food prices rose year-on-year 2.6 percent in June, with prices for vegetables falling 0.5 percent year-on-year.
Prices for non-food products increased 4.6 percent.
The ministry said public utility fares increased 4.7 percent in June, and prices for services, such as private-sector education fees, rose 5.3 percent.
Prices for hamburgers, one of the major service prices, dropped 10.4 percent, the ministry said.
The CPI, South Korea's leading inflation indicator, rose 4.5 percent in all of 1996, down from a 4.7 percent rise in 1995, the ministry said.
It said the CPI rise would be around or even below 4.5 percent this year.
